name: Grabbit
objective: Create a website to allow users to easily reserve items based on item category.
details: Created a full-stack application to allow users to create profiles, join families, add items to families, and reserve those items for periods based on their specified item category.
highlights: Built a full-stack category-based reservation application with a React + TypeScript frontend and a C# .NET backend.
Designed and implemented a REST API with CRUD operations, JWT-based authentication, and transactional database logic using EF Core and PostgreSQL.
Integrated frontend and backend using Axios and built a responsive UI with Tailwind.
learned: Gained experience with full-stack development, using C# with .NET, creating RESTful APIs, and integrating a frontend and backend using Axios.

name: Reelfindr
objective: Create a website to allow users to easily find, learn about, and comment on movies and add them to a personal watchlist.
details: Worked with a small team to create Reelfindr. Users can securely create accounts, search through the entire movie catalog, leave comments, and add movies to personal watchlists.
highlights: Built an accessible website that meets WCAG AA standards and can be used with screen readers.
Implemented secure user authentication and profile features.
Developed live commenting system for movies.
learned: Gained experience with full-stack React development, authentication, database integration with Convex, and collaborative team workflows.

name: Functional Electrical Stimulation Leg Device
objective: Create a device that connects to an app on the user's phone to detect critical gait events and trigger timed electrical impulses to enable smoother walking patterns.
details: I was the lead frontend designer for the companion app for the device. I am currently designing the app to be intuitive and user friendly, and to convey the critical information needed for this kind of medical aid device.

name: Badlang Compiler
objective: Build a MIPS compiler for the custom language Badlang.
details: Built a lexer, parser, name/type checking system, and code generator to translate Badlang into MIPS assembly. Badlang is a statically scoped language that supports arithmetic expressions, control flow, and functions. Implemented recursive descent parsing, a call stack for function execution, and meaningful error reporting.
highlights: Implemented detailed error reporting showing the error type, line, and characters involved in the error.
Implemented error aggregation to show related errors together for easy viewing.
Built the compilation pipeline from scratch to successfully convert a Badlang file into MIPS assembly.
learned: Gained deep understanding of language design, parsing techniques, error displaying, and scope management.

name: Mini Database
objective: Build a lightweight relational database system supporting basic SQL-like queries.
details: Implemented a simple in-memory database capable of executing simplified versions of core SQL commands such as SELECT and INSERT. Designed a custom parser and execution engine to interpret a minimal SQL-like language and perform basic table operations.
highlights: Created a query interpreter for a custom SQL-like syntax
Supported table creation, data insertion, and selection
Handled record storage and retrieval using efficient in-memory structures
learned: Gained experience with language parsing, data modeling, and understanding the execution model of database query engines.

name: Autodifferentiation
objective: Implement an efficient differentiation system using dual numbers.
details: Custom Python library supporting dual numbers for value and derivative computation. Includes arithmetic, trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic operations, making it useful for optimization and machine learning applications.
highlights: Implemented operator overloading to handle dual number arithmetic seamlessly
Supported chainable operations for derivatives of complex expressions
Designed to be easily integrable with other Python projects
learned: Gained experience with numerical methods, operator overloading, and designing reusable Python libraries.

name: Snake Rain
objective: Created a web-based puzzle game combining mechanics of Tetris and Snake for a unique gameplay experience.
details: Players control a snake-like block that falls and fits into a grid like Tetris. Implements collision detection, line clearing, and smooth controls using JavaScript and HTML/CSS.
learned: Improved skills in DOM manipulation, event handling, and game logic design.
